data.claim: Will Saturday's protests in France draw less than half last week's crowd?
data.resolution_source: French Interior Ministry national count of demonstrators for Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026, as published by the ministry or relayed from it by AFP, Le Monde or franceinfo
data.resolution_rule: Yes if the Interior Ministry's nationwide count of protesters in France for Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026, is below 275,000, which is half its count of 550,000 for Oct. 17. No if it is 275,000 or more. Use the latest full-day national figure the ministry publishes by 23:59 Paris time on Oct. 31, 2026; if it publishes only an intraday figure, use the latest one published by then. Ignore later revisions and any count by unions, organizers or independent counters. If the ministry publishes a national figure for Oct. 24, that figure settles the question whatever else happens. If it publishes none by the deadline: void if the national protest day was moved from Oct. 24 to a later date; otherwise Yes, including when the calls are withdrawn or banned or the protests are too scattered for a national count.

data.claim: Will Saudi Arabia's private businesses shrink this month?
data.resolution_source: S&P Global, Riyad Bank Saudi Arabia PMI press release for October 2026 (pmi.spglobal.com), expected around Nov. 3-4, 2026
data.resolution_rule: Yes if the headline seasonally adjusted Riyad Bank Saudi Arabia PMI for October 2026, as first published by S&P Global, is below 50.0. No if it is 50.0 or higher. Later revisions are ignored. If S&P Global has not published the October 2026 reading by the end of Nov. 5, 2026, the question is void.

data.claim: Will Trump and Putin meet in person by next month's China summit?
data.resolution_source: White House and Kremlin (kremlin.ru, Peskov or Ushakov) statements; Reuters and AP reporting
data.resolution_rule: Yes if, between Oct. 20 and Nov. 20, 2026, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin hold an in-person meeting or talks anywhere, including at the APEC leaders' summit in Shenzhen on Nov. 18-19. The meeting may be one-on-one or together with Xi Jinping or others in a three-way format. It counts if the White House or the Kremlin describes it as a meeting or talks between the two leaders, or if both Reuters and AP report that the two held a meeting or talks. It must be held apart from sessions, meals or photos open to all APEC leaders: a conversation during those does not count, whatever either side calls it. A handshake, greeting or brief exchange counts only if the White House or the Kremlin calls it a meeting or talks. Phone and video calls do not count. Reports published by Nov. 23 about a meeting held by Nov. 20 count. No if no qualifying meeting held by Nov. 20 is reported by Nov. 23, including if either leader skips the summit or leaves without one. Void if the APEC leaders' summit in Shenzhen is called off or postponed past Nov. 20 and no qualifying meeting has been held by then.

data.claim: Will America or Israel bomb Iran again before Thanksgiving?
data.resolution_source: Official statements by the US Department of Defense, US Central Command or the White House, or by the Israel Defense Forces or the Israeli Prime Minister's Office; or reporting by at least two of Reuters, the Associated Press and Axios.
data.resolution_rule: Yes if, between 2026-10-20T09:00Z and 2026-11-25T23:59Z, US or Israeli forces carry out at least one air, missile or drone strike on a target on Iranian territory: the mainland, Iranian-held islands, or ships moored at an Iranian port or base. A strike launched at such a target counts whether or not Iranian defences intercept it. The strike must be acknowledged by one of the named governments or reported as a US or Israeli strike by at least two of the named outlets, in their own reporting or citing US or Israeli officials; Iranian accusations alone do not count, nor do reports the outlets have retracted by the end of 2026-11-28. Not counted: blockade enforcement or other action against vessels at sea, including inside Iran's territorial waters; interception of Iranian missiles, drones or boats; strikes on Iranian-backed groups or Iranian assets outside Iran; cyberattacks; and sabotage or killings inside Iran that neither government acknowledges and the named outlets do not report as a US or Israeli strike. A strike before Nov. 3 counts the same as one after it. Acknowledgements and reports published up to the end of 2026-11-28 count for strikes within the window. If no qualifying strike in the window has been acknowledged or reported by the end of 2026-11-28, the question resolves No.

data.claim: Will Moody's keep France's credit rating where it is on Friday?
data.resolution_source: Moody's Ratings announcement on France at moodys.com, cross-checked with the Agence France Trésor's France credit ratings page and wire reports (Reuters, AFP).
data.resolution_rule: Yes if Moody's leaves France's long-term issuer rating at Aa3 in every announcement on France published by the end of Oct. 24, 2026 UTC, whatever it does to the outlook or review status, including when it publishes no rating action on France at its scheduled Oct. 23, 2026 review. No if, by the end of Oct. 24, 2026 UTC, Moody's announces any change to that rating, such as a cut to A1 or below, even if the change is later reversed. Void only if, by the end of Oct. 24, 2026 UTC, Moody's formally announces that it has moved the Oct. 23 review past Oct. 24, 2026 and has not changed the rating.

data.claim: Will Russia keep banning its oil refineries from selling diesel abroad?
data.resolution_source: Russian government decree published on government.ru or the official legal portal publication.pravo.gov.ru, or an official government or Deputy Prime Minister Novak announcement reported by Interfax, TASS, Reuters or Kommersant.
data.resolution_rule: Yes if, by 23:59 Moscow time on Nov. 1, 2026, the Russian government has adopted a decision extending past Oct. 31, 2026, to any later date, the temporary ban on exports of diesel fuel (with or without marine fuel and gasoil) by producers, so that the ban is in force on Nov. 1, as shown in a decree or an official announcement of the decision published by 23:59 Moscow time on Nov. 4, 2026. An extension still counts as yes if it keeps or widens exceptions: government-approved contracts, the volumes agreed with the U.S., intergovernmental agreements or supplies to Eurasian Economic Union states. A replacement regime that still forbids producers to export diesel without case-by-case government permission or a quota also counts as yes. Only the status on Nov. 1 counts: a later lifting does not change a yes. No if the producer ban lapses on Oct. 31 or is lifted earlier, so that on Nov. 1 producers may export diesel without case-by-case government approval; if the decision is adopted only after Nov. 1, even if it reimposes the ban; or if no decree or official announcement of an extension adopted by Nov. 1 is published by Nov. 4. Statements that an extension is being considered do not count. The separate ban on diesel exports by traders and small refineries, in force to Jan. 31, 2027, and the gasoline and jet fuel bans do not count either way.

data.claim: Will new US savings bonds pay at least 1.3% above inflation?
data.resolution_source: US Treasury savings bond rate announcement on TreasuryDirect (I bonds interest rates page or the accompanying press release) for Series I bonds issued Nov. 1, 2026 through Apr. 30, 2027.
data.resolution_rule: Yes if the announced fixed rate for Series I savings bonds issued from Nov. 1, 2026 through Apr. 30, 2027 is 1.30% or higher, up from 0.90% now. No if it is below 1.30%. Only the fixed rate counts. The inflation part, already set at 4.08% by the September report, and the total rate do not decide the question. The announcement is expected Oct. 30 or Nov. 2, 2026, because Nov. 1 is a Sunday; in 2025 it came on Oct. 31 when Nov. 1 fell on a Saturday. If Treasury corrects the announced rate by the end of Nov. 9, 2026, the corrected rate counts. If Treasury stops issuing Series I bonds and sets no rate for this period, the question is void. Otherwise, if Treasury has published no new fixed rate by the end of Nov. 9, 2026, the answer is No.

data.claim: Will French diesel stay nearly as expensive despite the government's cut?
data.resolution_source: The French Ministry of Ecological Transition's weekly note of average pump prices (national average price of gazole, all taxes included), for prices as of Friday, Nov. 6, 2026, usually published the following Monday. If no such note is published by Nov. 16, use the national average diesel price for Nov. 6 in the government's weekly transparency report on the stock release, if published by Nov. 16. If that is also missing, use the national average of official station price declarations on prix-ca
data.resolution_rule: Yes if the national average diesel price for Nov. 6, 2026 is 2.28 euros a litre or higher. That would be a fall of 5 cents or less from the 2.33 euros in the ministry note dated Oct. 9, 2026, two days after the cut was announced: less than half the low end of the promised 12 to 18 cents, and below even TotalEnergies' smallest pledge of 8 cents. No if it is below 2.28 euros. The first published figure counts; later revisions are ignored. If, by Nov. 6, the government has moved the start of discounted pump prices past Nov. 6 or cancelled the release, the answer is void when the price is 2.28 euros or higher and No when it is below.

data.claim: Will France's November strike draw fewer marchers than Saturday's protests?
data.resolution_source: French Interior Ministry nationwide count of demonstrators for the Nov. 5, 2026 inter-union day of strikes and marches (CFDT, CGT, FO, Unsa, FSU), as published by the ministry or reported from it by AFP, Le Monde, franceinfo or Le Figaro.
data.resolution_rule: YES if the Interior Ministry's nationwide demonstrator count for the Nov. 5, 2026 inter-union day, published by the end of Nov. 12, 2026 (Paris time), is below 550,000, the ministry's count for Oct. 17, 2026. NO if it is 550,000 or more, or if the ministry publishes no nationwide figure for the day by then. If the ministry publishes more than one nationwide figure for the day, use the latest published by Nov. 12. Union, organizer or independent counts and Paris-only or other partial figures do not count. The threshold stays 550,000 even if the ministry later revises its Oct. 17 figure. If the day is moved to another date no later than Nov. 6, 2026, use the ministry's count for that date. VOID only if the day is cancelled or moved to a date after Nov. 6, 2026.

data.claim: Will Iraq keep pumping about as much oil as in September?
data.resolution_source: OPEC Monthly Oil Market Report, November 2026 edition (scheduled for Nov. 11, 2026), table of OPEC crude oil production based on secondary sources (thousand barrels a day).
data.resolution_rule: Yes if Iraq's crude production for October 2026 in that table is at least 95% of Iraq's September 2026 figure as printed in the same table (that is, a fall of no more than 5% from September, using the September figure as revised in that edition). No if it is below 95%. Only the secondary-sources table in that edition counts, not Iraq's own reported figure (direct communication), any later OPEC revision, or any other agency's estimate. If OPEC has not published the November 2026 edition by Nov. 11, 2026, or that edition's table gives no October 2026 figure for Iraq, the question is void.

data.claim: Will Brazil keep paying diesel importers extra past mid-November?
data.resolution_source: Diário Oficial da União (in.gov.br), all editions including extra editions: Ministry of Finance ordinances (Portarias MF) under MP 1.391/2026, or any other federal act on the same subsidy; Finance Ministry and Agência Gov announcements as a cross-check only.
data.resolution_rule: Yes if, between Oct. 18 and Nov. 16, 2026, the Diário Oficial da União (any edition, including an extra edition) publishes a Ministry of Finance ordinance, or any other federal act such as a decree or medida provisória, that extends the additional subsidy for imported road diesel A created by Portaria MF 3.082 of Oct. 13, 2026 (R$1.40 a litre, valid 30 days from publication, about Nov. 12), or sets any new subsidy paid only on imported road diesel A, in either case in force on at least one day after Nov. 12, 2026. Any amount above zero counts, whether the top-up is renewed alone or folded into a combined rate that is higher for imported than for domestically produced road diesel. Only publication in the Diário Oficial counts; an announcement without it does not. The result is read on Nov. 19, 2026 from the Diário Oficial archive. No if no such act was published by Nov. 16, 2026, including when only the general subsidy paid to all producers and importers continues, or when the government ends the top-up early. Void if, before Nov. 12, 2026, the subsidy scheme of MP 1.391/2026 is rejected or suspended by Congress or a court.

data.claim: Will America let Hungary keep buying Russian oil for six more months?
data.resolution_source: US Treasury Office of Foreign Assets Control publications (licences, FAQs, recent actions), announcements by MOL or the Hungarian government, or reporting by Reuters, Bloomberg or AP of any of these.
data.resolution_rule: Yes if, by Nov. 23, 2026, the US Treasury has issued an authorisation for MOL, through a renewal or amendment of its licence or through a general licence, to keep buying crude from Lukoil or Litasco delivered through the Druzhba pipeline until at least May 21, 2027, without conditions that require MOL to cut those purchases, and has not revoked it by Nov. 23; or has lifted the US sanctions on Lukoil by Nov. 23 so that no licence is needed. A promise or agreement in principle that has not been issued does not count. The end date in the licence decides; only when no end date is published or reported does a renewal reported by MOL, the Hungarian government or one of the named outlets as lasting six months or more count as yes. Where reports of the terms conflict, the US Treasury's own terms prevail. Reports published by Nov. 26, 2026 count; if none by then reports such an authorisation, the answer is no. Otherwise no, including a lapse on Nov. 21, 2026 or extensions issued by Nov. 23 that run only to dates before May 21, 2027, such as a short stopgap.

data.claim: Will Korea's central bank hold off on raising rates in November?
data.resolution_source: Bank of Korea monetary policy decision announcement for its Monetary Policy Board meeting scheduled for Nov. 26, 2026 (bok.or.kr press release, published the same day), and any Bank of Korea announcement of a base rate change between Oct. 23 and Nov. 26, 2026.
data.resolution_rule: No if the Bank of Korea announces any rise in its base rate between Oct. 23 and Nov. 26, 2026, whether at its November meeting or at an unscheduled meeting. Otherwise Yes once the November decision is announced, whether it holds or cuts. The rate as announced on the decision day counts; later reversals do not change the result. If no November meeting has been held by Nov. 26, 2026 because it was moved later or called off, and no rise was announced in the window, the question is void.

data.claim: Will Indonesia's central bank hold off raising interest rates on Wednesday?
data.resolution_source: Bank Indonesia's press release on the result of its Board of Governors meeting ending Oct. 21, 2026, published at bi.go.id
data.resolution_rule: NO if Bank Indonesia announces an increase in the BI-Rate at any meeting, scheduled or unscheduled, between Oct. 17 and Oct. 21, 2026, even if it is later reversed. Otherwise YES if the BI-Rate announced after the Board of Governors meeting ending Oct. 21, 2026 is 5.75% or lower. Changes to the deposit or lending facility rates alone do not count. If the scheduled decision is not published by Oct. 21, 2026 and no increase has been announced in the meantime, the question is void.

data.claim: Will Ukraine's central bank raise interest rates again this month?
data.resolution_source: National Bank of Ukraine press release on its key policy rate decision, bank.gov.ua, published on the decision day (scheduled Oct. 29, 2026).
data.resolution_rule: Yes if the NBU Board's monetary policy decision announced on Oct. 29, 2026, or any key policy rate decision announced between the cutoff and Oct. 29, 2026, sets the key policy rate above 16.0% a year. The announced decision counts even if the new rate takes effect after Oct. 29 or is later reversed. No if every such decision keeps the rate at 16.0% or lowers it. Other tools, such as reserve requirements, the interest rate corridor or currency rules, do not count. If the scheduled meeting is postponed past Oct. 29, 2026 and no rate decision is announced by then, the question is void.

data.claim: Will Brazil keep paying its diesel subsidy in full after the vote?
data.resolution_source: Diario Oficial da Uniao (Brazil's official gazette, including extra editions): Ministry of Finance acts on the economic subsidy for road-use diesel A under MPs 1.363 and 1.391/2026, cross-checked with Ministry of Finance (gov.br/fazenda) announcements.
data.resolution_rule: Yes if the federal economic subsidy for road-use diesel A is in force at R$2.12 per liter or more on every day from Oct. 27 through Oct. 28, 2026, under Portaria MF 2.946/2026 or acts published in Diario Oficial da Uniao editions dated Oct. 17 through Oct. 28, 2026 (Brasilia time): a Ministry of Finance act, or a law or new provisional measure, and no act published by then sets a rate below R$2.12 for any day of the new period. A renewal published by Oct. 28 that applies back to the day after Portaria MF 2.946/2026 ends counts, as does an extension of that portaria at an unchanged rate. No if no such act appears in an edition dated by Oct. 28, including when a renewal is only announced, or if acts published by then leave the subsidy below R$2.12 per liter or out of force on any day from Oct. 27, or set a lower rate for any later day of the new period. Acts published after Oct. 28 do not change the result. The rate is the general subsidy paid to producers and importers (now R$1.12 plus R$1.00); the additional import-only subsidy under Portarias MF 2.813 and 3.082/2026 does not count toward it, nor do tax cuts, measures on petrol, ethanol or cooking gas, or Petrobras's own price changes.

data.claim: Will renting AI chips cost more in a month than now?
data.resolution_source: Silicon Data B200 Rental Price Index (ticker SDB200RT, Neo-Cloud segment), published daily at silicondata.com/products/silicon-index/b200 and on Bloomberg
data.resolution_rule: Yes if the Neo-Cloud index value for Friday, Nov. 13, 2026, as first published and read to the cent, is above 6.01 dollars per GPU-hour, its value for Oct. 16, 2026. No if it is 6.01 dollars or lower. Later revisions do not count. If no value for Nov. 13 is published by Nov. 21, use the value for the latest earlier day from Nov. 6 on that is published by then. Void if no value for any day from Nov. 6 to Nov. 13 is published by Nov. 21, or if Silicon Data changes its method in a way it says breaks comparison with Oct. 16.
